**Log Skeleton for the Order Fulfillment Process**

```python
{
    'equivalence': {
        ('RO', 'IC'),          # Every order that is received is invoiced (and vice versa)
        ('GSL', 'D')           # Shipping label is always generated when dispatched (and vice versa)
    },
    'always_before': {
        ('CA', 'RO'),
        ('RI', 'CA'),
        ('PI', 'RI'),
        ('QC', 'PI'),
        ('PO', 'QC'),
        ('GSL', 'PO'),
        ('D', 'GSL'),
        ('IC', 'D'),
        ('RP', 'IC')
    },
    'always_after': {
        ('RO', 'CA'),
        ('CA', 'RI'),
        ('RI', 'PI'),
        ('PI', 'QC'),
        ('QC', 'PO'),
        ('PO', 'GSL'),
        ('GSL', 'D'),
        ('D', 'IC'),
        ('IC', 'RP')
    },
    'never_together': set(),   # No mutually exclusive activities in the main happy path
    'activ_freq': {
        'RO': {1},
        'CA': {1},
        'RI': {1},
        'PI': {1},
        'QC': {1},
        'PO': {1},
        'GSL': {1},
        'D': {1},
        'IC': {1},
        'RP': {0, 1}           # Payment may not have been received yet at process end
    },
    'directly_follows': {
        ('RO', 'CA'),
        ('CA', 'RI'),
        ('RI', 'PI'),
        ('PI', 'QC'),
        ('QC', 'PO'),
        ('PO', 'GSL'),
        ('GSL', 'D'),
        ('D', 'IC'),
        ('IC', 'RP')
    }
}
```

This Log Skeleton encodes the linear happy-path control flow with strict precedence, direct succession, and single-occurrence constraints while allowing the final payment recording to be optional. All main activities are in equivalence with their logical counterparts and are bounded to exactly once per case. No activities are declared as mutually exclusive.
